item.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. Across two locally run open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks, and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals while retaining most repairs of violations. The directions of this tradeoff are partly implied by the rule; its magnitude depends on reviewer transitions and upstream proposal states. A prospective validation then gives the reviewer an explicit choice to retain, replace, or escalate. This eliminates correct-proposal corruption for Qwen, but Mistral still replaces all 48 correct proposals; Qwen also declines every welfare-only repair that Mistral frequently attempts. Thus interface design changes reviewer behavior but is not a model-independent safeguard. The result is not that restricted review is universally better. It is that reviewer competence, action interface, and binding jurisdiction jointly determine both the correction domain and the corruption surface.

item.title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
item.description: arXiv:2611.05391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not. We call this gap operational blindness. We introduce Agent Harness Awareness, a trust-separated design in which the host supplies a small, fresh, verified state snapshot before a consequential action while retaining measurement, enforcement, evaluation, and final dispatch authority. We test its tools-and-network instance with ToolRoute, a controlled isolation benchmark that holds the task and candidate semantics constant and varies the operational information available to the model. In a 216-decision ablation across GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.7 Flash, verified tool-health state reduced mean observable policy regret by 96.9% against a same-shape neutral control (4,252 ms to 131 ms) and raised single-dispatch completion from 69.4% to 95.8%. In a separate 27-decision end-to-end replication with live local TCP/HTTP execution, OpenTelemetry client spans, and Toxiproxy-injected faults, verified state reduced mean regret from 8,956 ms to 0 ms (zero excess observable operational cost) and completed the live action in 9/9 model-by-fault cases versus 5/9 for the neutral control. These studies establish the tools-and-network instance of Agent Harness Awareness: selected host telemetry materially improves pre-dispatch operational choice. Runtime state, hardware pressure, economics, retry-aware recovery, and heterogeneous selection remain open empirical extensions of the same architecture.

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.05392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal random variables. This unpredictability forces infrastructure orchestrators into a dilemma: under-provisioning risks mid-execution throttling and deadline violations, while over-provisioning wastes scarce edge or cloud capacity. Existing schedulers require a fully known pipeline graph, while edge resource-management methods rely on parametric or stationary demand models, and neither fits the unknown, non-stationary profiles of agentic pipelines. We formalize this setting as the uncertainty-aware agentic orchestration problem, where the goal is to reserve, at dispatch time, compute and bandwidth allocations that cover actual pipeline demands, and to verify that the pipeline can meet its deadline, each with a prescribed probability. We then propose Conformal Reservation for Orchestration (CRO), an online algorithm that translates a sliding window of past execution traces into dispatch-time resource allocations with finite-sample, distribution-free coverage guarantees via conformal prediction. Simulations over heterogeneous task mixes with multi-modal and heavy-tailed profiles show that CRO is the only evaluated method that simultaneously satisfies target probabilistic coverage across all risk levels while, among coverage-feasible methods, attaining the lowest over-reservation, roughly halving the resource waste of the Chebyshev-bound baseline.

item.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2611.05393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps. These signals trigger targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On the MEDAGENTSBENCH hard subset (862 questions across nine biomedical datasets), upfront retrieval provides little benefit, while challenge-aware in-between retrieval performs better; on a multi-specialist backbone it improves accuracy on 8 of 9 datasets and adds 6 percentage points over Challenger Only. Ablations indicate benefits from both retrieval timing and gap-specific query signals, and a live web-search experiment shows that the timing advantage persists across retrieval backends. For specialist recruitment, self-triggered adaptation is unreliable, whereas Challenger-triggered recruitment raises GPT-4.1-mini MedQA accuracy from 46% to 54%, with positive direction on all tested generalization datasets. Naively combining retrieval and specialist recruitment degrades performance, highlighting the need to coordinate adaptive intervention channels. These results show that when and why external resources are recruited is a key design choice in multi-agent medical reasoning.

item.title: Learning Implicit Solves for Dynamic Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.05439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity simulation of dynamical systems is central to scientific discovery and engineering design, yet remains computationally demanding. Here we introduce the Implicit Neural Operator Solver (INOS), which learns the implicit solve and encodes a time integrator. INOS pretrains a neural operator from static equilibrium solutions and reuses it within Newmark-$\beta$ integration. At each time increment, the integrator forms an effective equilibrium problem, the pretrained neural operator infers the next-step solution field, and the Newmark relations advance the dynamic state. Numerical examples in linear and nonlinear elastodynamics demonstrate accurate full-field predictions without dynamic trajectory supervision. Comparative results show that INOS, evaluated zero-shot, achieves higher predictive accuracy than neural solver baselines trained on dynamic simulations. In addition, INOS delivers over 4,600$\times$ speedup in nonlinear simulations over sequential classical finite-element solvers. INOS natively accommodates changes in dynamic conditions and enables reuse of the pretrained operator across spatial and temporal discretizations. Further evaluation demonstrates a stable million-step rollout. These findings establish INOS as a reusable neural implicit solver for accurate, efficient, and robust dynamic modeling.

item.title: Matched but Not Better: An Equivalence-Tested Benchmark of Quantum Machine Learning on Six Clinical Datasets and the QML-Health-READY Reporting Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.05442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background: Quantum machine learning (QML) is promoted for clinical prediction, but comparisons with classical models are rarely paired or tested for equivalence. Methods: We compared a quantum-kernel support vector machine (QSVM; 4 qubits, tuned bandwidth) and a variational quantum classifier (VQC) with five tuned classical models across six public clinical datasets. All models used identical four-component inputs and 25 cross-validation splits. Paired AUROC differences were assessed using a corrected resampled t-test, Holm-adjusted equivalence tests (margins: +/-0.02 and +/-0.05), and random-effects pooling. Ablation, noise, finite-shot, and implementation-fault analyses were conducted. We propose QML-Health-READY, an eight-domain reporting framework. Results: Neither quantum model significantly outperformed any classical comparator. Pooled across datasets, QSVM differed from the kernel-matched radial basis function (RBF) SVM by -0.006 AUROC (95% CI: -0.017 to +0.004), equivalent to +/-0.02. VQC differed from the best classical model by -0.007 (95% CI: -0.019 to +0.004). QSVM was equivalent to RBF SVM within +/-0.05 in four of six datasets but was significantly worse than the best classical model on NHANES 2017-18 (-0.076). A classically trivial product-state kernel performed as well as the entangling kernel. With depolarizing noise (p = 0.01) and 1,024 shots per kernel entry, QSVM AUROC decreased by 0.054 (95% CI: 0.036 to 0.071). Untuned bandwidth produced near-chance AUROC (0.48-0.59). Conclusions: Correctly configured quantum classifiers approached but did not exceed tuned classical models. Finite-shot estimation, rather than gate noise, was their main practical cost, while configuration errors could reverse conclusions. QML-Health-READY defines reporting requirements for credible claims.

item.title: The Confidence Score: a New Measure on Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.05528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Across a wide range of applications, kernel measures are used to tune hyperparameters, select among candidate kernels, and assess the suitability of kernels for specific learning tasks. For classification, kernel measures are used to predict which kernels may produce accurate kernel classifiers. Many existing kernel measures, such as alignment to the ideal kernel, are designed to reward kernels which captures all samples from the same class as similar. While effective in many settings, this requirement is unnecessarily restrictive for classification, where classes may exhibit substantial internal structure. In this work, the "Confidence Score", a new kernel measure, is proposed. Unlike alignment-to-the-ideal kernel measures, the Confidence Score measures the alignment between an encoding of the ground truth and that ground truth projected by the kernel, allowing kernels that preserve intra-class structure to achieve high scores. Through experiments, it is demonstrated that the Confidence Score exhibits a higher correlation with classification accuracy across a variety of kernels on both real-world and synthetic datasets, compared to select other kernel measures.

item.title: Recasting Visual Language Models as EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Neurodiagnostics
item.description: arXiv:2611.05538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Historically automated electroencephalography (EEG) systems was done using task-specific supervised models trained on purposely annotated data. A more recent modeling paradigm relies on creating a unified representation, or a 'foundation model', for multiple modality-specific tasks through large-scale domain-specific pretraining on the unannotated EEG signal. The quality of this unified representation directly depends on the availability of the modality-specific datasets. At the same time, generalist Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit broad few-shot learning capacities as well as good fine-tuning adaptability to different visual and language tasks. Can VLMs learn how to read and interpret EEG visually, emulating to a degree the way human clinicians inspect the EEG patterns? In this work we make a case that they can: we show that generalist VLMs without large-scale EEG pretraining perform competitively across a collection of clinical neuro-diagnostic tasks, can adapt to different tasks in a few-shot learning setting better than specialist foundation models, and exhibit better performance with model scaling when modality-specific models fail to exhibit.

item.title: Quasicrystals are Functionally Graded Materials
item.description: arXiv:2611.05478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasicrystals exhibit long-range order without translational periodicity, posing challenges to compute their electronic properties. Here we show that a quasicrystal can be represented exactly as a periodic approximant with a spatially graded phason, establishing a connection to functionally graded materials. Building on this connection, we develop a controlled quantum theory of quasicrystals. We derive a state-dependent control parameter governed by the quantum metric of local Bloch states, determining when finite approximations are reliable. We further construct a Hamiltonian that correctly predicts Bragg gap positions, quasimomentum equivalence, and quasiperiodic eigenstates to all orders in phason strain within a finite Fourier window. We verify the theory numerically and propose a diffraction-based experimental test of the gap shift induced by phason strain. Our framework opens a route to predicting the electronic structure and functional properties of quasicrystals using methods developed for functionally graded materials.

item.title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
item.description: arXiv:2611.05647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The thermal conductivities of (001) $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films deposited on $c$-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 $^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$ W/m$\cdot$K to 2.26 $^{+0.35}_{-0.40}$ W/m$\cdot$K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga$_2$O$_3$ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$-based electronic devices.

item.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
item.description: arXiv:2611.05654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections, formation-energy calculations and thermodynamic analysis, and data backup. By packaging this expertise as reusable agent skills, DefectSkills supports consistent workflow execution across agentic AI systems and reproducible defect calculations.

item.title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
item.description: arXiv:2611.05752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of $\approx$4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.

item.title: Local information processing capacity: anatomy of computation in neuromorphic systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.05959v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many neuromorphic systems possess rich internal computational structures shaped by their physical dynamics. However, existing metrics characterize only global computation, leaving these local structures unresolved despite their importance for system interpretation, optimization and miniaturization. Here, we introduce local information processing capacity (L-IPC), which represents individual dynamical states as vectors in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space and decomposes their computational properties through subspace projections onto nonlinearity orders and memory steps, with the residual quantifying computational irrelevance. Applied to three systems with comparable global capacities (an echo state network, an ion-gating reservoir and a spin-wave reservoir), L-IPC reveals markedly different distributions of computation, ranging from homogeneous to spatially, temporally and spectrally structured patterns. These local profiles further guide task-specific pruning, outperforming standard approaches at the same size in the structured systems. These results establish L-IPC as a general framework for anatomizing computation and guiding task-adaptive design in neuromorphic systems.

item.title: A Design Rule for Passive Reconfigurable Microwave Devices
item.description: arXiv:2611.06279v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every reconfigurable microwave device places a tuning element - a varactor, a diode, transistor, microelectromechanical or phase-change switch, a ferroelectric or liquid-crystal load - inside a fixed passive network. The network can make a small change of the element produce a large change of the response, and design practice often credits it with the device's tuning capability. This paper shows that a fixed, linear, passive network cannot add to that capability. Each tuning element carries a tuning budget, a dimensionless length computed from its own impedance trajectory, and a fixed passive network can transmit that budget or lose part of it, never enlarge it. The unit of the budget is the hyperbolic distance of the Smith chart: the distance from a match is the logarithm of the voltage standing-wave ratio, and the distance between two states sets their mutual mismatch and is the logarithm of their commutation quality factor. From one inequality we derive closed-form, ready-to-use limits for analog and digital phase shifters, true-time-delay lines, switches, attenuators, vector modulators, impedance tuners, tunable filters, reconfigurable antennas, metasurface cells and multiport networks; the two-state and attenuation limits are attained by explicit circuits, and the phase limit by a constant-loss trajectory. We introduce the $\Lambda$-chart, a Smith-chart companion on which budgets and requirements are read graphically, and apply it to four published microwave case studies.

item.title: Directional Control of Chiral Polymer Emission Dissymmetry by Plasmonic Metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.06400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Circularly polarized (CP) emission is central to next-generation photonic and optoelectronic technologies, yet simultaneously controlling its directionality, intensity, and handedness remains a major challenge. Advances in molecular and materials design have enabled strong chiral light-matter interactions and large dissymmetry between opposite CP states. However, conventional thin-film architectures provide limited control over the angular distribution of CP emission and often exhibit strongly angle-dependent chiral emission. Metasurfaces, on the other hand, offer powerful control over emission directionality and polarization, but have predominantly been explored with intrinsically achiral emitters. For the first time, we integrate organic chiral polymer thin films with planar chiral plasmonic metasurfaces to enhance chiral light-matter interactions while controlling the directionality and angular dependence of chiral emission. Using angle-resolved Stokes Fourier polarimetry, we show that metasurface coupling produces directional emission, near-normal dissymmetry factors exceeding 0.7, and, remarkably, direction-dependent reversal of the emission handedness at fixed molecular stereochemistry.

item.title: Stochastic Ising networks with asymmetric and time-delayed interactions
item.description: arXiv:2607.15215v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stochastic Ising networks are widely used to describe collective dynamics in complex systems and to compute, yet physical implementations of these networks often contain both asymmetric interactions and nonzero signal propagation times that fall outside conventional theories of their behavior. Here, we study stochastic Ising networks with asymmetric and time-delayed interactions motivated by experimental observations in coupled superparamagnetic tunnel junctions. Time delay fundamentally reshapes the dynamics induced by antisymmetric couplings, producing strong oscillatory temporal correlations consistent with experiment. Sufficiently long delays strongly suppress the non-uniformity of steady-state probability distributions, a behavior explained by an exponential suppression of the first-order equal-time cross-correlation between pairs of spins. Residual non-uniformity is due to the equal-time cross-correlation mediated by a third spin that contributes only at higher order in the coupling strength. These relatively featureless probability distributions coexist with pronounced delayed temporal correlations, distinguishing them from equilibrium high-temperature behavior. We further show analytically that these delay-induced near-uniform distributions emerge in a broad class of stochastic networks that lack symmetry-breaking bias fields. Introducing symmetry-breaking bias fields restores a strong dependence of the steady state on interactions with qualitatively modified behavior. Simulations of networks with five coupled spins demonstrate that these effects persist beyond minimal systems with only two spins.

item.title: 学校不用 Gemini 就不能用搜索？谷歌新规引发美国政界人士批评
item.description: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，谷歌当地时间周二宣布，使用其 K-12 教育软件的学校，除非选择启用 AI 工具， 否则将无法使用谷歌搜索（Google Search） 。这一决定随即引发强烈反对。 谷歌教育业务副总裁克里斯 · 菲利普斯（Chris Phillips）向《纽约时报》表示，“搜索与 AI 已经深度整合”。因此，如果一所学校不选择启用 Gemini 等 AI 工具，学生将无法使用搜索功能，并会看到一条由学校提供的提示信息，告知他们该功能不可用。 尽管谷歌选择在美国中期选举日当天公布这一消息，但仍有多位倾向民主党的政界人士专门发声，对此表达担忧。 美国佛蒙特州联邦参议员伯尼 · 桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）在 X 平台发文，指责谷歌的做法属于“敲诈勒索”。他写道：“谷歌正在威胁学校：如果你们阻止学生使用 AI，我们就切断你们使用谷歌搜索的权限。这不是热爱，这是敲诈。立即暂停人工智能发展。” 康涅狄格州联邦参议员理查德 · 布卢门撒尔（Richard Blumenthal）也在 X 平台表示，谷歌“更关心的是如何将 Gemini 强行引入学校，而不是如何帮助学生取得成功”。 美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）前主席、长期主张打击垄断行为的莉娜 · 汗（Lina Khan）也谴责谷歌的决定，认为此举涉嫌反竞争。 她写道：“这凸显了让一个不受监管的垄断企业控制关键服务所带来的危险。多家法院已经认定谷歌违反了反垄断法，而这一最新举措表明，该公司并未因此有所收敛。” 纽约市市长佐兰 · 马姆达尼（Zohran Mamdani）则指责谷歌形成垄断，并表示：“任何企业都不应该拥有决定我们如何教育孩子的权力。” 搜索功能是学生获取信息的重要工具，但教育工作者担心，谷歌搜索内置的 AI 概览功能可能会让学生不再主动寻找答案，而是直接依赖 AI 提供结果。对于数百万被要求使用 Chromebook 和谷歌教育工具的学生而言，改用其他搜索引擎并不是一个简单的解决办法。 谷歌表示，正在为学生账户开发一项名为“引导式学习”（Guided Learning）的搜索功能。该功能旨在引导学生逐步解决问题或查找信息，而不是直接给出答案。 例如，如果学生在解答一道数学题时遇到困难，该功能可能会提示学生回顾指数除法的相关规则，而不是直接给出计算结果。 IT之家注意到，面对外界质疑，谷歌在 X 平台发文回应称，公司听取了教育工作者的意见，已经将 AI 产品的访问权限默认关闭，并强调学校可以分别选择启用 Gemini、Gemini Notebook 和谷歌搜索。 谷歌在声明中表示：“我们知道，学校担心学生利用 AI 走捷径完成作业，也知道学校希望掌握相关工具的使用权限。这正是我们今天推出这些调整的原因，目的是回应过去几个月从教育工作者那里收集到的反馈。我们将继续与教育工作者深入沟通，确保为学校提供更多选择、更完善的控制权限，以及更有助于学习的搜索体验。”

item.title: 机器人格斗表演为什么不如去年有看头了？宇树科技 CEO 王兴兴回应
item.description: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据澎湃新闻报道，如今一个很有趣的现象是，今年机器人格斗表演的观赏性反而不如去年。宇树科技创始人兼 CEO 王兴兴在第九届虹桥国际经济论坛人形机器人与具身智能产业创新发展合作论坛上表示，机器人自主格斗是宇树 2025 年提出的构想，到现在已经过去一年多。 王兴兴认为，有一个很有趣的现象是，现在格斗表演的观赏性反而不如去年， 原 因是过去机器人稳定性差 ， 打斗的对抗感更强 ；如今机器人稳定性大幅提升，无论受到怎样击打都站得很稳，倒地、摔倒的场面变少了。 IT之家从原报道获悉，王兴兴在会上还介绍了宇树科技基于端到端世界模型实现的机器人全自主格斗，机器人实时采集画面，由模型直接推理决策。

item.title: 华为余承东：鸿蒙电脑迈过百万台门槛，是新的起点
item.description: IT之家 11 月 5 日现场消息，在今天的华为擎云 2026 鸿蒙办公产业峰会现场，华为终端平板与 PC 产品线总裁朱懂东宣布， 鸿蒙电脑累计发货量破百万 。 华为终端官方也转发了这一全新成就。IT之家注意到，华为常务董事、产品投资评审委员会主任、终端 BG 董事长余承东随后发文，表示： 鸿蒙电脑迈过百万台门槛，是新的起点 。感谢大家的选择和支持 [抱拳] 今天，面向企业办公的华为擎云 HM650 系列、鸿蒙电脑企业版也来了 。未来我们会继续和伙伴们一起，不断丰富应用、打磨体验！ 延伸阅读 鸿蒙电脑于 2025 年 5 月 19 日在成都首次发布，首批产品为 HUAWEI MateBook Pro 与 HUAWEI MateBook Fold 非凡大师，两款产品均搭载基于开源鸿蒙打造的 HarmonyOS 5，是首个从操作系统内核层面重构的国产电脑。 华为擎云是华为面向政企市场的商用终端品牌。本次亮相的擎云 HM650 系列是华为首款鸿蒙台式机，搭载麒麟 X90 处理器，运行 HarmonyOS 7，整机国产化率达到 100%，定位政企办公市场，此前已在华为全联接大会上公开展示。 擎云 HM650/HM650g 提供 16GB 内存、512GB 固态硬盘等多种配置，正式开售时间为 2026 年 10 月 15 日，仅面向政企客户，不在电商平台及线下体验店销售。硬件方面，该系列采用双层散热架构，支持麒麟 X90 处理器以 40W TDP 运行，并支持设备、数据及应用互联，提供小艺任务、小艺慧记和小艺深度研究等功能。 随着台式机产品落地，鸿蒙电脑目前已覆盖传统笔记本、折叠屏电脑和台式机三种形态，产品线包括 MateBook Fold 系列、MateBook Pro S 系列、MateBook Pro 系列以及 MateBook 系列等。鸿蒙电脑生态已拥有 21000+ 独立应用，覆盖办公、AI、教育、娱乐、内容创作等多个核心场景。 此外，华为终端 BG 平板与 PC 产品线总裁朱懂东在本次峰会上还预告，华为将推出一款新的颠覆性创新鸿蒙电脑产品，将于下周开始预热；同时官宣鸿蒙电脑将在 2026 年内支持侧载，开放本地安装应用。 在 2026 年 6 月的 HDC 2026 上，朱懂东曾透露鸿蒙电脑市场表现超出预期，其中 MateBook Fold 在折叠电脑市场占据 70% 份额，轻薄本（8000 元以上价位）市场份额为 12%。

item.title: macOS 藏着“脏话识别系统”，苹果词典分级机制被曝光
item.description: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，挪威开发者 Helge Sverre 于 11 月 3 日发布博文，通过逆向分析 macOS 私有框架 Lexicon.framework ， 发现苹果输入法内置“脏话识别系统”。 开发者指出在 macOS 系统 ~/Library/Keyboard/ 目录下，存在名为 VulgarWordUsage.db 的本地数据库，其数据结构可按“应用、收件人、词语、读音”记录用户使用脏话的情况。IT之家附上相关截图如下： 开发者挖掘 macOS 15.6 的系统词典，发现苹果使用 Lexicon.framework 框架对词条进行分级和主题标注。在美式英语词典约 19.9 万个词条中，约 4,271 个词条配有分级标记，主要分为“粗俗”（vulgar）、“冒犯”（offensive）和“敏感”（sensitive）三类内容，并进一步标注排泄、身体部位、侮辱、疾病、药物、政治、宗教、性、暴力、武器等主题。 用途方面，开发者认为该机制并非用于直接审查或禁止用户输入，主要用于改进键盘自动更正和联想建议，例如避免系统在用户未主动输入时推荐不合适的词汇。 值得注意的是，被标记并不等于被屏蔽。用户仍可输入相关词语，系统通常也不会将其强行改写；其作用更接近于降低这些词在 QuickType 候选栏中的主动出现概率。 参考 I Dumped Apple's Fucking Word List
